doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Recording constantly
summary: Allen mentions two new recordings and says Sun Ra recorded everything daily, leaving huge stacks of tapes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: I understand you just finished another recording?
Yeah, two. [to off camera] How many recordings did we do? Two?
Does a Sun Ra recording session go fairly quickly compared to a lot of bands?

Oh boy we got so many stuff. He’d be anywhere and record. Like we’d be at rehearsal and he’d be recording. So you’d get it right, it would come out one way and we’d go in the studio it would come out another way. Same song. You see? So he’d be recording everything. That’s why so many tapes and music because every day, seven days a week. Now you put a year on that and seven days a week is a lot of recordings. And you’ve got stacks and stacks of tapes. I’ve got garbage bags full of tapes. Man you know those big industrial bags? Full of tapes.
